per_case.playbook: 1) Immediately isolate WEB-BO-01 from the network (quarantine VLAN / disable uplinks). 2) Preserve forensic images (memory + disk) before rebuilding. 3) Terminate the active SSH session from 185.220.101.4 and kill related processes. 4) Rotate credentials for the 'deploy' account and any accounts that could reach root. 5) Block 185.220.101.4 at the perimeter firewall. 6) Hunt for lateral movement — check other hosts for SSH connections from 185.220.101.4 or from WEB-BO-01. 7) Rebuild the host from known-good image; do not attempt to clean in place given root-level compromise.

Immediately isolate FILE-BO-01 from the network. Block external IP 91.240.118.172 at the edge firewall. Reset credentials for svc_backup and NORTHSTAR\svc_backup accounts. Preserve the host for forensic analysis (the tar archive and shadow deletion indicate active anti-forensics). Investigate the Finance share for data loss scope and check for exfiltration to external destinations. Review for lateral movement from this host to other systems.

Isolate WS-NKAPOOR-01 from the network immediately. Preserve forensic images before remediation. Block outbound connections to 45.83.221.30 at the firewall. Investigate the originating NORDSTAR\nkapoor credentials for compromise and force credential reset. Determine the initial access vector (WMI lateral movement) and check for lateral movement to other hosts. Escalate to incident response for full malware analysis and host rebuild.
No action required. This is benign user activity (password typo). No isolation or blocking warranted. Continue routine monitoring.

Block external IP 45.83.220.5 at the perimeter firewall (FW-BO-EDGE) and add it to the blocklist/threat-intel feed. Confirm no additional Nikto scan sources are targeting WEB-BO-01, verify the phpMyAdmin endpoint is not deployed, and monitor for follow-up scans from related IP ranges.

BLOCK the external C2 IP 45.83.221.30 at the perimeter firewall/egress filter and add it to the threat intelligence blocklist. Simultaneously ISOLATE the internal host 10.20.3.44 (source of the beacons) for forensic analysis and remediation, as it is the compromised asset. Investigate the initial infection vector and check for lateral movement or data exfiltration originating from 10.20.3.44.

BLOCK the external IP 198.51.100.77 at the edge firewall. Verify whether user 'vhales' has a legitimate VPN account and whether the failed attempts indicate a mistyped password vs. a credential-stuffing attack. Review VPN logs for any subsequent successful authentication from this IP or other suspicious accounts. If confirmed malicious, add the IP to the blocklist and monitor for related source IPs.

Immediately isolate DC-BO-01 from the network (disable network access via switch port / VLAN quarantine). Preserve forensic images before remediation. Rotate all credentials and service accounts that could be affected by the harvested lsass/NTLM secrets, especially those of jbiros and any accounts with access to this DC. Investigate the source IP 10.20.3.70 for the initial access vector and check for lateral movement to other hosts. Hunt for the m.exe binary across the environment and remove it. Rebuild DC-BO-01 from known-good baseline and restore from backup after validating integrity.

Immediately isolate SQL-BO-01 from the network. Preserve forensic images (disk/memory) before remediation. Disable the newly created 'svc_sql' account and any other accounts created by the attacker. Rotate credentials for the 'sa' service account and all accounts with access to this SQL instance. Block the source IP 10.20.3.62 at the edge and hunt for lateral movement from SQL-BO-01 to other hosts. Patch the SQL Server xp_cmdshell/remote-code-execution vector, and review all accounts with elevated privileges on the instance.

Isolate WS-LCHEN-01 from the network immediately. Preserve the compromised user account NORTHSTAR\lchen credentials and force a password reset. Capture memory and disk forensics, then remove the malicious Word document and PowerShell artifacts. Block outbound connection to 193.32.162.44 and cdn-update-center.net at the firewall. Conduct a hunt for the initial malicious document across other user workstations and review for lateral movement.

Isolate MAIL-BO-01 from the network immediately. Preserve logs for forensics. Investigate the postfix configuration for open-relay misconfiguration or compromise (unauthorized credentials, trojaned mail scripts, botnet agent). Block outbound port 25 at the edge to stop the spam bleed. Rotate credentials for any accounts that authenticated through this host. Audit for other hosts using the same mail server and report the abuse to the upstream provider / mx01.example.net operator.

Isolate BKUP-BO-01 from the network immediately. Preserve forensic images before remediation. Investigate the svc_upd account for compromise and rotate its credentials. Remove the 'SysSync' scheduled task and delete C:\Windows\Temp\sync.exe. Perform full endpoint malware scan, review other accounts the compromised service account had access to, and hunt for lateral movement originating from this host.

Isolate WS-JDIAZ-01 from the network immediately. Preserve the LSASS dump and procdump binary as evidence. Revoke and rotate credentials for the NORTHSTAR\jdiaz account and any privileged accounts. Investigate the parent svc.exe process and its parent PID 7710 for the initial access vector. Perform threat hunt for lateral movement using harvested credentials and check for any C2/beaconing activity once the host is quarantined.

Immediately isolate APP-BO-02 from the network (disconnect/vLAN quarantine). Block egress to 45.83.221.30 at the edge and add it to the firewall deny-list. Kill the active reverse shell session and any processes spawned by the 'ubuntu' account. Preserve forensic images before remediation. Rotate credentials for the 'ubuntu' account and any other accounts that accessed the host. Investigate the downloaded lin.sh payload for persistence mechanisms and scope for lateral movement. Rebuild the host from known-good media rather than cleaning in place, given the confirmed root-level compromise.

BLOCK the external source IP 185.220.101.4 at the perimeter firewall (already partially denying). Add an explicit deny/IPS block rule for 185.220.101.4/32 on inbound SSH (port 22). Verify WEB-BO-02 has not been compromised (confirm all root logins failed, review for any successful login or account enumeration). Recommend enforcing key-based SSH auth, disabling root SSH login, and deploying fail2ban / rate-limiting on sshd. Monitor for continued probing from associated Tor exit-node ranges.

Block external IP 103.152.90.14 at the edge firewall/IDS immediately. Investigate WEB-BO-02 for signs of successful injection (check for any 200 responses with sensitive data, review WAF rules, ensure parameterized queries). Since attacks returned 500, confirm the web app is not fully bypassed, but prioritize blocking the attacker source and monitor for follow-up attempts from related ranges.

Block external IP 194.26.29.88 at the perimeter firewall/IPS immediately. Escalate the confirmed webshell compromise on internal host WEB-BO-02 (10.20.1.11) for isolation, forensic imaging, and removal of the uploaded shell.php file; rotate web application credentials and review WAF rules.

BLOCK the external IP 91.240.118.172 at the edge firewall/IPS immediately. Since the brute-force did not succeed (all attempts failed), no host isolation is strictly required, but verify FILE-BO-01 and 10.20.2.20 for any residual activity. Enforce account lockout policies, MFA for RDP/admin accounts, and consider restricting RDP exposure via VPN or network segmentation. Monitor for follow-up attempts from related IPs.

Isolate host 10.20.3.62 from the network immediately. Preserve forensic images and perform memory/disk forensics to identify Emotet persistence and additional indicators. Block egress to 193.32.162.44 and the domain cdn-update-center.net at the edge firewall. Hunt for lateral movement and C2 beaconing from the host, rotate credentials for any accounts used on it, and initiate full malware removal / OS reinstallation per incident response runbook.

Block external IP 80.94.95.226 at the perimeter firewall (already denying, but add explicit blocklist). Add signature/rule to detect and rate-limit further scanning from this source. Review target host 10.20.0.10 for any signs of successful exploitation, though current evidence indicates all attempts were denied.

Block external IP 222.186.42.7 at the edge firewall/IPS immediately. Add/verify IDS/IPS signatures for RDP brute-force detection. Rotate credentials for the 'amorgan' account and review for any later successful logons. Monitor internal hosts 10.20.3.91 and WS-AMORGAN-01 for follow-up activity. Ensure RDP is not exposed to untrusted networks and enforce MFA + account lockout policies.

No action required. This is expected benign activity — a Microsoft 365 sign-in originating from Microsoft's own IP range. No need to block the IP or isolate any host. Consider tuning the signature to reduce informational alert noise if volume is high.

Isolate host 10.20.4.15 from the network immediately. Preserve forensic images, revoke and rotate the svc_backup_agent credentials, and investigate the host for malware/C2 implants. Block outbound SMB to 10.20.2.20 and audit the destination for data exfiltration. Review adjacent hosts for lateral movement originating from 10.20.4.15.
No action required. Confirm the alert is a false positive. No need to isolate or block. Continue routine monitoring; the observed activity is standard Windows Update behavior.

No action required. Confirm SCAN-BO-01 is an authorized vulnerability scanner in asset inventory. Optionally tune the IDS signature to suppress known-internal Nessus scanner user-agents to reduce alert noise.

No action required. Dismiss the alert as a likely false positive. If the alerting system continues to fire for WEB-BO-02, verify the sensor configuration and alert correlation rules to prevent alert fatigue.
No action required. DNS-BO-01 is operating as a normal DNS resolver. Continue routine monitoring; no isolation or blocking is warranted.

No action required based on available telemetry. Recommend verifying that the telemetry ingestion pipeline is operational, since all four tables are empty — a new alert exists but no corresponding local evidence is present. Re-run triage once database connectivity and alert ingestion are confirmed, or correlate the alert with external threat intelligence once the reputation API key is configured.
No action required. Dismiss the alert as a false positive / benign activity. No host isolation or IP block is warranted.
No action required. This is benign ordinary service use. Continue routine monitoring; no isolation or blocking warranted.

No action required. This is benign user activity (occasional password mistype followed by successful login and normal application startup). No isolation or blocking warranted. Continue routine monitoring.
